methodology: Prometheus v2 (Puter 240K LOC pattern extraction → 333 Rust/WASM mapping)
summary: 10 concrete Puter architectural patterns (microkernel registry, hot-load, actor-auth, context isolation, service lifecycle, useapi DI, event pub-sub, worker system, filesystem abstraction, runtime export) with explicit Rust/WASM/WebRTC/CRDT mappings for 333 platform.

keyFindings.applicableTo333: 100% (all patterns port via sealed trait abstraction + CRDT edges)
keyFindings.implementationWeeks: 6-8 (parallel: 4 service lifecycle + 3 DI runtime + 2 event infra)

patterns.description: Puter's 226-service registry uses singleton store (service_name → Service instance map). Dynamic lookup at runtime. No compile-time checking.

333Mapping.trait: sealed ServiceRegistry<S: Service> { register(name: &str, factory: Box<dyn Fn() -> S>); resolve(name: &str) -> Option<S>; }
333Mapping.implementation: Hashmap<String, Arc<dyn Service>> backed by RwLock for concurrent access. Factory pattern delays instantiation until first resolve().
333Mapping.rustFeature: sealed trait pattern (pub trait sealed { } impl<T> sealed for T where T: Service {})
333Mapping.testingStrategy: Unit: mock registry with 3 dummy services. Integration: spawn 333 signaling + state + presence, verify cross-service DI.
333Mapping.crdt_integration: Registry mutation → CRDT Or-Set edge (add service, remove service) for distributed cluster sync.

patterns.description: Puter allows .js modules to be loaded at runtime (UIService extends via plugin hooks). No verification of plugin API contracts. Uses eval().

333Mapping.trait: pub trait PluginManifest { fn exports() -> HashMap<&'static str, VersionSchema>; fn validate() -> Result<(), SchemaError>; }
333Mapping.implementation: Load WASM modules from kubeadm sidecar (read from ConfigMap). Verify against Zod schema pre-instantiation. No eval; only static dispatch.
333Mapping.rustFeature: wasmtime::Instance + arc-swap for zero-copy hot-reload. Manifest versioning via SemVer constraints.
333Mapping.testingStrategy: Load 2 plugins: Ledger (exports ledger_query) + AuthHandler (exports middleware). Verify exports match manifest. Inject bad plugin, verify rejection.
333Mapping.crdt_integration: Plugin metadata → CRDT json-like field (version, hash, enabled_nodes[]). Cross-node plugin enable/disable via CRDT merge.
333Mapping.riskLevel: MEDIUM (WASM instantiation overhead; mitigate: lazy-load on-demand)

patterns.description: Puter's UIService receives user input → routes to handlers. No explicit capability model. Auth checks scattered. ACL is string-based.

333Mapping.trait: pub trait AuthActor { fn capability(&self) -> Capability; fn enforce(req: &Request) -> Result<(), PermissionDenied>; }
333Mapping.implementation: Each peer (browser, node) = Actor with signed certificate (node_id + pubkey + capabilities[]. Capability enum: SignCRDT, ModifyLedger, SpawnWorker. Verify signature on every RPC.
333Mapping.rustFeature: ed25519 signing (ring crate). Capabilities as bitfield (u64). Certificate caching with TTL. Revocation via CRDT TombstoneGC.
333Mapping.testingStrategy: Actor A (Signaling capability) tries to modify Ledger → reject. Actor B (Ledger+Signaling) → accept both. Certificate rotation (rekey) → verify all connections re-handshake.
333Mapping.crdt_integration: Capability revocation → CRDT edge (REVOKES, GRANTS). Cross-node enforcement: peer X broadcasts revoke(peer Y, ledger_write). All peers merge via CRDT quorum.
333Mapping.riskLevel: MEDIUM (key management; mitigate: use kubeadm Secret + mTLS termination at Traefik)

patterns.description: Puter's Workers (FileWorker, DecryptWorker) execute in shared JS context. No isolation. Leaks possible via closure capture.

333Mapping.trait: pub trait SandboxContext { fn execute(script: &SignedScript) -> Result<Output, SandboxError>; fn memory_limit(bytes: u64); fn cpu_timeout(ms: u64); }
333Mapping.implementation: Use kubeadm ephemeral containers (Pod with volumeMount=/dev/null, no network). Alternatively: wasmtime.Store with resource limits. Script signed with author's ed25519. Output JSON serialized, CRDT-wrapped before return.
333Mapping.rustFeature: wasmtime ResourceLimiter + TLS cert validation for author. Output postcard-serialized to prevent serde gadgets.
333Mapping.testingStrategy: Worker_A (LEDGER_COMPUTE) → modifies ledger CRDT, returns signed result. Worker_B (FILESYSTEM) → reads config, returns hash. Verify both output signatures match author.
333Mapping.crdt_integration: Worker output tagged with (worker_id, frame, signature, data). Merged into CRDT as append-only log. Determinism: hash of output used as CRDT value hash.
333Mapping.riskLevel: HIGH (ephemeral containers = Pod overhead; mitigate: pre-warm container pool, use wasmtime for lighter sandbox)

patterns.description: Puter defines Service base class with init() → listeners() → close(). No enforcement. Cleanup race conditions. UIService overrides all 3.
patterns.puterLocation: src/service/service.js (2.4K LOC, base) + src/ui/service.js (26K LOC, override)

333Mapping.trait: pub trait Service: Send + Sync { async fn init(&self) -> Result<()>; async fn shutdown(&self) -> Result<()>; fn dependencies(&self) -> Vec<&'static str>; }
333Mapping.implementation: Enum ServiceState { Created, Initializing, Ready, Shutting, Closed }. State machine checked at every transition. Shutdown waits for in-flight requests (graceful). Registry owns Arc<Service>; when all Arc drops = service freed.
333Mapping.rustFeature: tokio::sync::broadcast for shutdown signals. Dependency DAG resolved at startup; cycle detection via topological sort.
333Mapping.testingStrategy: Start Service A (depends B) → B not ready → A init fails. Start B then A → both Ready. Shutdown B → A transitions to Degraded (or fails fast). All state transitions logged to CRDT event stream.
333Mapping.crdt_integration: Service state changes → CRDT events (ServiceInitialized, ServiceShutdown). Each node tracks peer service states in Or-Set (node_id, service, state).
333Mapping.riskLevel: MEDIUM (deadlock if dependency cycle undetected; mitigate: static check at compile-time via procedural macro)

patterns.description: Puter's useapi() function accepts string name of service. Returns service instance. Zero type safety. Services register manually.

333Mapping.trait: pub trait Provide { type Output: Send + Sync; fn provide() -> Self::Output; } pub fn use_service<S: Provide>() -> S::Output { S::provide() }
333Mapping.implementation: Compile-time DI via Rust type system (no strings). Services register via global Setup ctor (called once on main.rs). Zod-style schema enforcement: use_service::<SignalService>() verifies schema before return.
333Mapping.rustFeature: procedural macros: #[derive(Service)] auto-impl Provide trait with schema validation. TypeId hashing replaces string lookup.
333Mapping.testingStrategy: Test 1: use_service::<SignalService>() → returns correct instance. Test 2: call method that type-checks (e.g., signal.broadcast()). Test 3: schema mismatch → compile error (no runtime cost).
333Mapping.crdt_integration: DI container state (all Services + versions) serialized into CRDT as immutable snapshot at startup. Cross-node DI audit: all peers verify same schema versions.

patterns.description: Puter's services emit events (.emit('load'), .on('close')). Event handler registry is global. No backpressure. Lost events on slow handler.

333Mapping.trait: pub trait EventBus { fn publish<E: Event>(&self, event: E); fn subscribe<E: Event, H: Handler<E>>(handler: H) -> Subscription; }
333Mapping.implementation: tokio::sync::broadcast channel per event type. Handlers registered in HashMap<EventType, Vec<Arc<dyn Handler>>>. Backpressure via bounded channel (capacity=1000). Slow handlers time out after 5s → logged to CRDT.
333Mapping.rustFeature: async/await for handler execution. Event serialization via serde_json (or postcard for perf). CRDT tagging: (event_id, peer_id, frame, payload_hash).
333Mapping.testingStrategy: Emit 100 events in 10ms → all 3 subscribers receive in-order. Subscribe late → receive no prior events (only new). Unsubscribe during emit → no deadlock.
333Mapping.crdt_integration: Each event tagged with ULID (monotonic) + peer_id. CRDT Or-Set merges events across nodes. Determinism: event order deterministic within same frame (causal consistency).
333Mapping.riskLevel: MEDIUM (unbounded event queue on slow handler; mitigate: metrics + circuit breaker)

patterns.description: Puter spawns Web Workers for compute-heavy tasks (image decode, crypto). No job tracking. Worker crashes are silent.

333Mapping.trait: pub trait WorkerPool { fn submit<T: Task + 'static>(&self, task: T) -> Result<JobHandle<T::Output>, QueueFull>; fn poll_result(handle: &JobHandle<T>) -> Poll<Result<T::Output, TaskError>>; }
333Mapping.implementation: kubeadm DaemonSet (2 replicas) + mTLS. Each Pod has rayon thread pool (workers=num_cpus). Task submitted via gRPC → worker process → result → CRDT signed output. Job tracking via Neo4j: Job node (job_id, status, worker_pod_id, result_hash).
333Mapping.rustFeature: tokio task-local storage + tracing for observability. Result signed via worker private key. Dead worker detected via liveness probe (healthz endpoint).
333Mapping.testingStrategy: Submit 10 tasks (compute primes, hash data, decrypt). Verify all results. Kill 1 worker mid-task → job retries on peer. Crash 2 tasks → both report error via CRDT.
333Mapping.crdt_integration: JobStatus CRDT (job_id → {status, worker_id, result_frame, signed_output}). Replicas merge via majority voting (if 2 workers claim different result, reject both).
333Mapping.riskLevel: HIGH (distributed job tracking under clock skew; mitigate: ULID-based job IDs + causal commit on result write)

patterns.description: Puter defines VirtualFS (legacy, 14K LOC) + FileSystem (new, 8K LOC). Dual APIs. Some services use old, some new. Migration incomplete.

333Mapping.trait: pub trait FsBackend: Send + Sync { async fn read(&self, path: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>>; async fn write(&self, path: &str, data: &[u8]) -> Result<()>; async fn list(&self, path: &str) -> Result<Vec<FsEntry>>; }
333Mapping.implementation: Single impl KubeadmLocalPath (uses kubeadm local-path-provisioner). Sealed trait prevents drift. All paths go through unified VFS tree (no mixed calls). CRDT-aware: writes tagged with (writer_peer_id, frame, path_hash). Concurrent writes to same path: CRDT LWW or quorum votes on winning version.
333Mapping.rustFeature: tokio-uring for async I/O (Linux only; fallback to tokio::fs). Path normalization via path-absolutize. Writes checksum'd before persist.
333Mapping.testingStrategy: Test 1: peer A writes /ledger.json, peer B reads → receives latest. Test 2: A + B write /ledger simultaneously → CRDT picks one (deterministic tie-break). Test 3: list / → includes all entries.
333Mapping.crdt_integration: Filesystem state = CRDT Map<path, {data_hash, writer_id, frame, checksum}>. When path written: broadcast (path, new_hash) to all peers; they fetch full data via BitTorrent-like block exchange if missing.
333Mapping.riskLevel: HIGH (concurrent write semantics complex; mitigate: strong consistency model + quorum reads)

patterns.description: Puter's UIService exports properties/methods on-the-fly (.expose() pattern). No versioning. API breaks silently. No backwards compatibility.

333Mapping.trait: pub trait PublicApi: Sized + Send + Sync { fn api_version() -> SemVer { SemVer::new(0,1,0) } } #[macro_export] macro_rules! export_api { ($ty:ty) => { ... } }
333Mapping.implementation: Procedural macro #[export_api(version = "1.0.0")] generates stable ABI wrapper. WASM export table versioned. Old API versions kept for 2 minor releases (deprecation path). Version negotiated at connection handshake (peer announces its api_version, other peer adapts).
333Mapping.rustFeature: Semver checking at runtime. ABI stability via wasm-bindgen with explicit version markers. Type erasure via serde_any for cross-version compat.
333Mapping.testingStrategy: Test 1: Export Service v1.0 with method foo(). Upgrade to v1.1 (add bar(), keep foo()). Old client connects → gets foo() only. New client → gets both. Test 2: Upgrade to v2.0 (remove foo()) → old client fails gracefully with version mismatch error.
333Mapping.crdt_integration: API schema versioned in CRDT (peer_id → {api_version, exports_hash}). Cross-node version audit: all peers log (peer X exports v1.0, peer Y exports v2.0) to Neo4j. Mismatch triggers warning to operator.
333Mapping.riskLevel: MEDIUM (SemVer discipline required; mitigate: CI check that forces version bump on API change)

crossCuttingConcerns.crdt_integration: All 10 patterns tagged with CRDT mutations (Or-Set for registries/services, LWW for state, append-only log for events). Determinism via frame-based consensus.
crossCuttingConcerns.testingStrategy: Unit tests (mock registry, DI container). Integration tests (3-node cluster: signal event via P7 → all nodes receive via CRDT merge). Load tests (1000 events/sec × 3 patterns).
crossCuttingConcerns.rolloutOrder: P1(Registry) → P6(DI) → P5(Lifecycle) → {P2,P3,P4,P7,P8} parallel → P9(FS) → P10(Export)
crossCuttingConcerns.estimatedTotalWeeks: 6-8 (if parallel sprints: registry+DI=2wk, auth+lifecycle+event=2wk, worker+sandbox+fs=2wk, export=1wk)

successCriteria: All 10 patterns have sealed trait boundaries (no inheritance, composition-only)
100% of patterns tested with multi-node CRDT merges (determinism verified)
Zero runtime type erasure in P6 DI (compile-time checked)
P9 filesystem concurrent writes use CRDT quorum (no lost updates)
P10 API export uses SemVer + version negotiation (no silent breakage)

risks.risk: CRDT merge ordering complexity (P7 events, P9 filesystem)
risks.mitigation: Use frame-based linearization + ULID for total order. Test with network partition simulation.

risks.risk: Worker pool job tracking under Byzantine fault (P8)
risks.mitigation: Require 2/3 worker agreement on result hash before CRDT commit. Slashing for equivocation.

risks.risk: Filesystem LWW vs. quorum consistency model (P9)
risks.mitigation: Explicit choice at design phase. LWW = low latency (risk lost writes). Quorum = strong consistency (slower). Document tradeoff.

recommendations: Adopt P1+P6 first (foundation). Complete in week 1-2 to unblock 333 service initialization.
P2 (hot-load) can be deferred to week 6 if kubeadm deployment sufficient.
P9 (filesystem) is critical blocker for ledger persistence. Prioritize after P5.
